newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northwest products notionally steady late.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northwest products notionally steady late.

text.p: U.S. Northwest products prices were notionally steady with levels from late last week, traders said, with little fundamental news ahead of the long holiday weekend next week.
Traders said refineries appeared to run normally, including Arco's Ferndale, Wash., plant, which generated higher offers last week on rumours of an operational problem.
Gasoline prices in the Northwest will rise in early October on the switchover to winter-formula grades, which require more ethanol blend in the Northwest.
"You'll see the prices jump up eight or nine cents a gallon," one trader forecast.
Regular unleaded gasoline was assessed at 67 cents to 67.50 cent a gallon.
Low sulphur diesel ranged 67 to 68 cents a gallon, while jet fuel was seen around 71.50/72.50 late Monday.
Premium gasoline was seen about 6.5 cents higher than regular, traders said.
